summary: Know Your Pharmacy - A citizen-centric mobile app for India that helps users verify pharmacy and pharmacist details, check pharmacist presence at dispensing counters, and generate complaints to appropriate authorities when pharmacists are absent. Built with Flutter, Node.js backend, and PostgreSQL.
architectural_notes: Flutter mobile app with Node.js/Express backend and PostgreSQL database
Offline-first design: core flows work without network, reports queued locally
Optional authentication with guest mode for anonymous complaints
State management using Provider or Riverpod for separation of UI and business logic
Camera and GPS permissions requested explicitly with user consent
Encrypted local storage for sensitive report data
Modular architecture: separate UI, state, data layers for maintainability
Translation-ready architecture with string externalization for Hindi/English support
Email client integration for pre-filled complaint submission to authorities
Configuration-driven authority lists (state-specific) stored in backend
known_issues: "Get Started" button on onboarding screen is not triggering navigation to home screen

existing_features.title: Create onboarding flow with three screens: (1) app purpose explanation (public interest, patient safety), (2) legal disclaimer stating the app does not certify/de-license pharmacies, only assists in collecting information and preparing complaints, and (3) terms and privacy policy acceptance. Show on first launch only.

Build home screen with four navigation cards: 'Check pharmacy & pharmacist', 'Report an issue', 'How to complain / Know your rights', and 'My reports' (visible when user is logged in or has local reports).

Implement 'Check pharmacy' screen with fields: pharmacy name (text), address (text with optional GPS capture button), state (dropdown with Indian states), optional drug license number (text). Include 'Next: Check pharmacist' button that advances to pharmacist verification.

Build 'Check pharmacist' screen with fields: pharmacist name (text), registration number (text), state of registration (dropdown). Include photo capture button for pharmacist name display board and placeholder for future QR scanning. Validate registration number format (non-empty, alphanumeric). Display message: 'Verification is indicative only. Official verification is done by State Pharmacy Council / PCI / relevant authority.'

Create pharmacist presence check questionnaire with questions: (1) 'Is the registered pharmacist physically present at the counter right now?' (Yes/No/Not sure radio buttons), (2) 'Who is actually dispensing medicines?' (dropdown: Registered pharmacist / Other staff / I am not sure), (3) 'How long did you observe the situation?' (dropdown: 0-5 min / 5-15 min / >15 min). Include buttons to capture multiple photos (entrance, counter, pharmacist info), capture GPS location, and auto-generate timestamp.

Build 'Report details' screen that pre-fills pharmacy details, pharmacist details, date/time, GPS location, and photos from previous steps. Add issue type selection (multi-select checkboxes: Pharmacist absent, Pharmacist details not displayed, Suspected fake pharmacist, Others with text field). Include optional user contact fields: name, phone number, email. Generate structured complaint summary object for storage and export.

Implement 'Submit complaint' screen that displays state-appropriate authorities based on pharmacy state and issue type. Show recommended authorities: State Drug Controller, State Pharmacy Council, CDSCO, Consumer forum. For each authority, display email, phone, and website. Provide 'Send email complaint' button that opens device email client with pre-filled recipient, subject line format 'Complaint regarding pharmacist absence / pharmacy operations – [State], [City]', and structured complaint summary in body. Include 'Open complaint website' button that launches browser.

Build education module with static content pages explaining: (1) role and responsibilities of registered pharmacist in India, (2) importance of pharmacist presence for safe dispensing, (3) basic pharmacy regulations in simple language. Include FAQ section with questions: 'What should be displayed in a legal pharmacy?', 'Can a pharmacy run without pharmacist?', 'What evidence should I keep when I complain?'. Content should be stored in backend as markdown or JSON for easy updates.

Implement 'My Reports' screen showing list of user's reports (for logged-in users) or local reports (guest mode). Display summary for each: pharmacy name, date, issue type, status (Draft, Email sent). Support export (as text or formatted complaint), edit (navigate back to report details), and delete actions. For guest mode, store reports in local device storage until app data is cleared.

Add optional user authentication supporting email/phone registration and guest mode. Guest users can submit anonymous complaints but must provide contact details in report if authority requires it. Logged-in users have their contact details pre-filled. Authentication should be simple and not required for core app functionality.

Implement offline-first architecture where all core flows (pharmacy check, pharmacist verification, presence check, report creation) work without network. Queue report submissions locally when offline and sync to backend when network becomes available. Only authority routing and opening external links require network. Show clear network status indicators.

Structure frontend for multilingual support with English as implemented language and architecture ready for Hindi translation. Use translation keys throughout UI instead of hardcoded strings. Store all user-facing text in a translations file that can be extended with Hindi translations later. Use English for all UI elements in initial implementation.

Ensure app is optimized for low-end Android devices with minimal network usage. Keep bundle size small, implement image compression for captured photos, use efficient list rendering for reports, and minimize backend API calls. Design clean, intuitive UI with clear icons suitable for users with varying technical literacy.

Implement privacy and security measures: request explicit permissions for location and camera with clear explanations, minimize data collection to only necessary fields, encrypt sensitive stored data on device, and allow users to delete their data. Include clear privacy policy during onboarding.
Verify that the useOnboarding hook correctly persists completion state to localStorage and that App.tsx properly reads this state to conditionally show the onboarding flow

Add 'I don't know' checkbox option to the Check Pharmacist screen that allows users to skip entering pharmacist name and registration number fields when they don't have this information. When checked, disable the name and registration number input fields and allow navigation to the next step without validation.

Update the Report Details screen and complaint email formatting to handle cases where pharmacist name and registration number are not provided. Display 'Not available' or 'Unknown' for missing pharmacist details in the report summary and email body.

Update the i18n translations file to include new translation keys for the 'I don't know' checkbox label and help text explaining that users can skip pharmacist details if they are not displayed at the pharmacy.

Create a new 'Regulatory Bodies' page accessible from the Education section or main navigation that displays comprehensive information about Indian pharmacy regulatory authorities including: Pharmacy Council of India (PCI), all state pharmacy councils, Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO), state drug controllers, and relevant consumer forums.

For each regulatory body listed on the page, display: full official name, brief description of their role and jurisdiction, contact email address, phone number (if available), and official website URL. Format contact information clearly with icons for email, phone, and web links.

Create a frontend query hook (similar to useEducationContent) to fetch regulatory bodies information from the backend, with proper loading and error states. Support filtering by state if needed for displaying state-specific councils.

Update the i18n translations file to include all text for the Regulatory Bodies page including: page title, section headings, body descriptions, field labels (Email, Phone, Website), and any explanatory text about the role of each regulatory authority type.

Add a navigation link to the Regulatory Bodies page in the main Layout component navigation menu, positioned near the Education link. Also add a reference or link from the Education page to the Regulatory Bodies page for discoverability.

Update RegulatoryBodyCard.tsx component to display full address field when available, showing it below the role description and above contact information. Format the address with appropriate spacing and icon (location pin icon).

Update i18n translations file to add translation keys for all new content including: section headers ('nationalBodies', 'stateCouncils', 'consumerForums'), section descriptions ('nationalBodiesDescription', 'stateCouncilsDescription', 'consumerForumsDescription'), field label for 'address', and updated role descriptions for all regulatory bodies with complete text as provided in the data.
